sentences.text: Virender Singh, Judge (oral)

Applicant, Prem Chand, has filed the present bail application, under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Cr. P.C.) for releasing him, on bail, during the pendency of the trial, in case FIR No. 285 of 2022, dated 2.12.2022, under Section 20 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substance Act (hereinafter referred to as the ND & PS Act), and under Sections 181 .
and 196 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the M.V. Act'), registered with Police Station, Sadar, District Bilaspur, H.P 2.

entities.text: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substance Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The applicant has pleaded the fact that he is innocent person and has falsely been implicated in the present case.

3. As per the applicant, the contraband, which has been shown to be recovered from his possession,
does not fall within the commercial quantity.

Asserting this fact, a reference has been made to the report of State Forensic Science Laboratory and it has been prayed that the applicant is in judicial custody and no useful purpose would be served by keeping him in judicial custody.

4. To buttress his contention, it has also been argued by learned counsel for the applicant, that chances of commencement of trial and its conclusion in near future are not so bright and the investigation in the present case is complete.
5. Apart from this, the applicant, through his counsel Mr. Rajiv Rai, Advocate, has given certain undertakings, for which, he is ready to abide by, in case, he is released on bail.

6. As per the averments of the bail application, the applicant has also tried his luck by moving bail application No. 101 of 2023, before the learned Special Judge, Ghumarwin, District Bilaspur, which was dismissed on 9.5.2023.
7.
On these submissions, a prayer has been made to allow the bail application.

.

sentences.text: When put to notice, the police has filed the status report, disclosing therein, that on 02.12.2022 HC Chaman Lal was on patrolling alongwith other police officials in government vehicle No. HP 606678.

When the police party was at NH154 at place near Prem Sagar Hotel and was checking the vehicles, at about 02.05 pm, one vehicle No. HP34C9197 (Bolero) r being drivern by its driver from Ghagas side towards Bilaspur and came there.
HC Chaman Lal stopped the vehicle for checking.
Bolero driver stopped the vehicle on the kuccha portion of the road.
On inquiry, the driver disclosed his identity as Prem Chand (applicant).
Applicant was asked to show the documents.
Accused had shown R.C., but disclosed that he is not having any other documents.
When the police party had shown intention to check the vehicle, the accused got scared and tried to avoid checking of the vehicle.
The police got suspicion that there might be some stolen substance or forest produce in the vehicle.
Efforts were made to associate independent witnesses.
At a distance of 20 feet from the spot, two persons were found, who were asked to be the witnesses.
In their presence, checking of Bolero vehicle was done.
On checking the vehicle from the dicky of the vehicle, a pink coloured packet was found alongwith other articles.
On checking the packet, contraband was found wrapped in a polythene.
Same was weighed on electronic weighing machine and its weight came out to be 1.034 kg.

9. The contraband was taken into possession and FIR was .
registered.
Applicant was arrested.
Applicant remained in police custody and presently is in judicial custody.

8. Apart from this, it has also been mentioned in the status report that another FIR No.
211/2012,dated 20.11.2012, under Sections 342,323, 376, 363, 382 IPC has been registered against the applicant in Police Station, Manali.
9. The present case is also stated to be fixed for 21.6.2023 for prosecution evidence, before the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Bilaspur.
10. On all these submissions, a prayer has been made to dismiss the application.

11. The perusal of report of State Forensic Science Laboratory, which has been placed on record,
shows that the total weight of parcel is 1.086 kg.
The weight of carry bag & parcel cloth is 0.086 kg.
Weight of exhibit with polythene wrappers is 1.006 kg.
Weight of polythene wrappers is 0.015 kg and actual weight of exhibit is 0.991 kg.

Meaning thereby, the said contraband, which is stated to be recovered from the possession of the applicant, does not fall within the definition of 'commercial quantity' and the same falls within the 'intermediate quantity'.
12. This fact has also not been disputed by the learned Additional Advocate General.
As such, it can be said that the rigors of Section 37 of the ND &PS Act are not applicable.

Since the rigors of .
Section 37 of the ND & PS Act are not applicable in this case, therefore, the presumption of innocence is still available to the applicant.
as pre trial punishment is prohibited under the law.

sentences.text: The chances of the conclusion of the trial against the accused in his near future are not very bright, therefore, no useful purpose would be served by keeping him in judicial custody.

14. So far as, the registration of another case against the applicant is concerned, this fact is also not sufficient to take away the presumption of innocence, as, admittedly, in that case, no punishment has been awarded to the applicant.
Mere registration of another case, does not take away the presumption of innocence.
As such,the bail application cannot be rejected as a matter of punishment, as pretrial punishment is prohibited under the law.
15. Considering all these facts, this Court is of the view that the bail application is liable to be allowed and is accordingly allowed.

16. The applicant is ordered to be released on bail in case FIR No. 285 of 2023, dated 2.12.2022,
under Section 20 of the NDPS Act, and under Sections 181 and 196 of the M.V.Act, registered with Police Station, Sadar, District Bilaspur, H.P. on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.
70,000/, with one surety in the like amount, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court.

sentences.text: 17. Any of the observations made herein above shall not be taken as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case as these observations are confined only to the disposal of the present bail application.
18. It is made clear that the respondentState is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case, any of the bail conditions is violated by the bail applicant.

19. The Registry is directed to forward a soft copy of the bail order to the Superintendent of District & Open Air Jail, Bilaspur, through email,with a direction to enter the date of grant of bail in the e prison software.

20. In case, the applicant is not released within a period of seven days from the date of grant of bail,
the Superintendent of concerned jail is directed to inform this fact to the Secretary, DLSA, Bilaspur.
